page: Microsoft Azure M128bds_3_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs derived from 64 physical Intel Xeon 8473C cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a cache configuration of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 105 MB L3 cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for hardware-accelerated matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 2794.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.83 GB of RAM per core, and includes 6144 GB of local storage with premium block storage capabilities.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with read-only small block, read-only large block, and write large block operations all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded processing is highly efficient, as demonstrated by top-tier results in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark database operations. The server also achieved top-tier throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the average range, though Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores remain strong. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds for prompt processing and text generation across 7B and 70B models consistently rank in the top 25%.

Given the high density of memory and the inclusion of 6.1 TB of local storage, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets without the overhead of external storage latency. The lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but the presence of Intel AMX instructions allows for strong CPU-based LLM inference. The server is designed for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data-intensive enterprise applications, and high-throughput web serving.
